settingItems.description:
Aligns infill, bridge, ironing and surface fill directions to follow the model's orientation on the build plate.
When enabled, directions rotate with the model to maintain optimal strength characteristics.
settingItems.label: Align infill direction to model

settingItems.description:
This factor affects the amount of material for bottom solid infill.

The actual bottom solid infill flow used is calculated by multiplying this value with the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.
settingItems.label: Bottom surface flow ratio

settingItems.description: This option will auto-detect narrow internal solid infill areas. If enabled, the concentric pattern will be used for the area to speed up printing. Otherwise, the rectilinear pattern will be used by default.
settingItems.label: Detect narrow internal solid infills

settingItems.description: Insert solid infill at specific layers. Use N to insert every Nth layer, N#K to insert K consecutive solid layers every N layers (K is optional, e.g. '5#' equals '5#1'), or a comma-separated list (e.g. 1,7,9) to insert at explicit layers. Layers are 1-base
settingItems.label: Insert solid layers

settingItems.description: Purging after filament change will be done inside objects' infills. This may lower the amount of waste and decrease the print time. If the walls are printed with transparent filament, the mixed color infill will be seen outside. It will not take effect, un
settingItems.label: Flush into objects' infill

settingItems.description: Speed of gap infill. Gap usually has irregular line width and should be printed more slowly.
settingItems.label: Gap infill

settingItems.description: Connect an infill line to an internal perimeter with a short segment of an additional perimeter. If expressed as percentage (example: 15%) it is calculated over infill extrusion width. Orca Slicer tries to connect two close infill lines to a short perimete
settingItems.label: Sparse infill anchor length

settingItems.description: Connect an infill line to an internal perimeter with a short segment of an additional perimeter. If expressed as percentage (example: 15%) it is calculated over infill extrusion width. Orca Slicer tries to connect two close infill lines to a short perimete
settingItems.label: Maximum length of the infill anchor

settingItems.description: Automatically Combine sparse infill of several layers to print together to reduce time. Wall is still printed with original layer height.
settingItems.label: Infill combination

settingItems.description: Don't support the whole bridge area which make support very large. Bridges can usually be printed directly without support if not very long.
settingItems.label: Don't support bridges

settingItems.description: Enable support generation.
settingItems.label: Enable support

settingItems.description: Purging after filament change will be done inside objects' support. This may lower the amount of waste and decrease the print time. It will not take effect, unless the prime tower is enabled.
settingItems.label: Flush into objects' support

settingItems.description: Support layer uses layer height independent with object layer. This is to support customizing Z-gap and save print time. This option will be invalid when the prime tower is enabled.
settingItems.label: Independent support layer height

settingItems.description: Use this setting to rotate the support pattern on the horizontal plane.
settingItems.label: Pattern angle

settingItems.description:
Line pattern of support.

The Default option for Tree supports is Hollow, which means no base pattern. For other support types, the Default option is the Rectilinear pattern.

NOTE: For Organic supports, the two walls are supported only with the Hollow/Def
settingItems.label: Base pattern

settingItems.description: Spacing between support lines.
settingItems.label: Base pattern spacing

settingItems.description: Spacing of bottom interface lines. Zero means solid interface.
settingItems.label: Bottom interface spacing

settingItems.description: Z gap between the object and the support bottom. If Support Top Z Distance is 0 and the bottom has interface layers, this value is ignored and the support is printed in direct contact with the object (no gap).
settingItems.label: Bottom Z distance

settingItems.description:
Density of internal solid infill for Elephant foot layers compensation.
The initial value for the second layer is set.
Subsequent layers become linearly denser by the height specified in elefant_foot_compensation_layers.
settingItems.label: Elephant foot layers density

settingItems.description:
Maximum layer height for the combined sparse infill.

Set it to 0 or 100% to use the nozzle diameter (for maximum reduction in print time) or a value of ~80% to maximize sparse infill strength.

The number of layers over which infill is combined is derived
settingItems.label: Infill combination - Max layer height

settingItems.description: Height of the first layer. Making the first layer height thicker can improve build plate adhesion.
settingItems.label: First layer height

settingItems.description: The height of the beams of the interlocking structure, measured in number of layers. Less layers is stronger, but more prone to defects.
settingItems.label: Interlocking beam layers

settingItems.description: Slicing height for each layer. Smaller layer height means more accurate and more printing time.
settingItems.label: Layer height

settingItems.description: Enable this to get precise Z height of object after slicing. It will get the precise object height by fine-tuning the layer heights of the last few layers. Note that this is an experimental parameter.
settingItems.label: Precise Z height

settingItems.description:
Start height of the scarf.
This amount can be specified in millimeters or as a percentage of the current layer height. The default value for this parameter is 0.
settingItems.label: Scarf start height

settingItems.description: How many layers of skirt. Usually only one layer.
settingItems.label: Skirt height

settingItems.description:
Minimum Z-layer height.
Also controls the slicing plane.
settingItems.label: Minimum Z height

settingItems.description: The number of layers on which the elephant foot compensation will be active. The first layer will be shrunk by the elephant foot compensation value, then the next layers will be linearly shrunk less, up to the layer indicated by this value.
settingItems.label: Elephant foot compensation layers

settingItems.description:
This option enables the generation of an extra bridge layer over internal and/or external bridges.

Extra bridge layers help improve bridge appearance and reliability, as the solid infill is better supported. This is especially useful in fast printers, whe
settingItems.label: Extra bridge layers (beta)

settingItems.description:
This factor affects the amount of material on the first layer for the extrusion path roles listed in this section.

For the first layer, the actual flow ratio for each path role (does not affect brims and skirts) will be multiplied by this value.
settingItems.label: First layer flow ratio

settingItems.description: Whether to apply fuzzy skin on the first layer.
settingItems.label: Apply fuzzy skin to first layer

settingItems.description: Acceleration of the first layer. Using a lower value can improve build plate adhesion.
settingItems.label: First layer

settingItems.description: Speed of solid infill part of the first layer.
settingItems.label: First layer infill

settingItems.description: Jerk for the first layer.
settingItems.label: First layer

settingItems.description: Line width of the first layer. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.
settingItems.label: First layer

settingItems.description: The minimum wall width that should be used for the first layer is recommended to be set to the same size as the nozzle. This adjustment is expected to enhance adhesion.
settingItems.label: First layer minimum wall width

settingItems.description:
Density of the bottom surface layer. Intended for aesthetic or functional purposes, not to fix issues such as over-extrusion.
WARNING: Lowering this value may negatively affect bed adhesion.
settingItems.label: Bottom surface density

settingItems.description: Combine multiple brims into one when they are close to each other. This can improve brim adhesion.
settingItems.label: Combine brims

settingItems.description: Generate interlocking beam structure at the locations where different filaments touch. This improves the adhesion between filaments, especially models printed in different materials.
settingItems.label: Use beam interlocking

settingItems.description: The distance from the boundary between filaments to generate interlocking structure, measured in cells. Too few cells will result in poor adhesion.
settingItems.label: Interlocking depth

settingItems.description: Expand the first raft or support layer to improve bed plate adhesion.
settingItems.label: First layer expansion

settingItems.description:
The geometry will be decimated before detecting sharp angles. This parameter indicates the minimum length of the deviation for the decimation.
0 to deactivate.
settingItems.label: Brim ear detection radius

settingItems.description:
Maximum angle to let a brim ear appear.
If set to 0, no brim will be created.
If set to ~180, brim will be created on everything but straight sections.
settingItems.label: Brim ear max angle

settingItems.description:
This factor affects the amount of material for brims.

The actual brim flow used is calculated by multiplying this value by the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

Note: The resulting value will not be affected by the first-layer flo
settingItems.label: Brim flow ratio

settingItems.description: A gap between innermost brim line and object can make brim be removed more easily.
settingItems.label: Brim-object gap

settingItems.description: This controls the generation of the brim at outer and/or inner side of models. Auto means the brim width is analyzed and calculated automatically.
settingItems.label: Brim type

settingItems.description:
When enabled, the brim is aligned with the first-layer perimeter geometry after Elephant Foot Compensation is applied.
This option is intended for cases where Elephant Foot Compensation significantly alters the first-layer footprint.

If your current setup
settingItems.label: Brim follows compensated outline

settingItems.description: Distance from model to the outermost brim line.
settingItems.label: Brim width

settingItems.description: Brim width of prime tower, negative number means auto calculated width based on the height of prime tower.
settingItems.label: Brim width

settingItems.description: Enabling this option means the width of the brim for tree support will be automatically calculated.
settingItems.label: Auto brim width

settingItems.description: Temperature difference to be applied when an extruder is not active. The value is not used when 'idle_temperature' in filament settings is set to non-zero value.
settingItems.label: Temperature variation

settingItems.description: When interface-layer temperature boost is active, set the nozzle back to print temperature at the start of the prime tower so it cools down during the tower.
settingItems.label: Cool down from interface boost during prime tower

settingItems.description: This option will drop the temperature of the inactive extruders to prevent oozing.
settingItems.label: Enable

settingItems.description:
Speed of the externally visible bridge extrusions.

In addition, if Slow down for curled perimeters is disabled or Classic overhang mode is enabled, it will be the print speed of overhang walls that are supported by less than 13%, whether they are part of
settingItems.label: External

settingItems.description: Enable this option to slow printing down for different overhang degree.
settingItems.label: Slow down for overhang

settingItems.description: Speed of the first layer except the solid infill part.
settingItems.label: First layer

settingItems.description: Travel speed of the first layer.
settingItems.label: First layer travel speed

settingItems.description: Speed of inner wall.
settingItems.label: Inner wall

settingItems.description: Speed of internal bridges. If the value is expressed as a percentage, it will be calculated based on the bridge_speed. Default value is 150%.
settingItems.label: Internal

settingItems.description: Speed of internal solid infill, not the top and bottom surface.
settingItems.label: Internal solid infill

settingItems.description: Print speed of ironing lines.
settingItems.label: Ironing speed

settingItems.description:
This setting adds an extra wall to every other layer. This way the infill gets wedged vertically between the walls, resulting in stronger prints.

When this option is enabled, the ensure vertical shell thickness option needs to be disabled.

Using lightnin
settingItems.label: Alternate extra wall

settingItems.description: Detect the overhang percentage relative to line width and use different speed to print. For 100%% overhang, bridge speed is used.
settingItems.label: Detect overhang walls

settingItems.description: Detect thin walls which can't contain two line widths, and use single line to print. Maybe not printed very well, because it's not a closed loop.
settingItems.label: Detect thin walls

settingItems.description: Infill area is enlarged slightly to overlap with wall for better bonding. The percentage value is relative to line width of sparse infill. Set this value to ~10-15% to minimize potential over extrusion and accumulation of material resulting in rough top su
settingItems.label: Infill/Wall overlap

settingItems.description: Acceleration of inner walls.
settingItems.label: Inner wall

settingItems.description:
Filament to print inner walls.
"Default" uses the active object/part filament.
settingItems.label: Inner walls

settingItems.description:
This factor affects the amount of material for inner walls.

The actual inner wall flow used is calculated by multiplying this value by the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.
settingItems.label: Inner wall flow ratio

settingItems.description: Jerk of inner walls.
settingItems.label: Inner wall

settingItems.description: Line width of inner wall. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.
settingItems.label: Inner wall

settingItems.description:
This value governs the thickness of the external (visible) bridge layer.
Values above 1.0: Increase the amount of material while maintaining line spacing. This can improve line contact and strength.
Values below 1.0: Reduce the amount of material while adj
settingItems.label: Bridge flow ratio

settingItems.description:
Enables gap fill for the selected solid surfaces. The minimum gap length that will be filled can be controlled from the filter out tiny gaps option below.

Options:
1. Everywhere: Applies gap fill to top, bottom and internal solid surfaces for maximum stre
settingItems.label: Apply gap fill

settingItems.description:
Controls the density (spacing) of internal bridge lines.
Internal bridges act as intermediate support between sparse infill and top solid infill and can strongly affect top surface quality.

- Higher than 100% density (Recommended Max 125%):

settingItems.label: Internal bridge density

This value governs the thickness of the internal bridge layer. This is the first layer over sparse infill so increasing it may increase strength and upper layer quality.
Values above 1.0: Increase the amount of material while maintaining line spacing. This
settingItems.label: Internal bridge flow ratio

settingItems.description: Use scarf joint to minimize seam visibility and increase seam strength.
settingItems.label: Scarf joint seam (beta)

settingItems.description:
If enabled, bridge extrusion uses a line height equal to the nozzle diameter.
This increases bridge strength and reliability, allowing longer spans, but may worsen appearance.
If disabled, bridges may look better but are generally reliable only for shorter

If enabled, internal bridge extrusion uses a line height equal to the nozzle diameter.
This increases internal bridge strength and reliability when printed over sparse infill, but may worsen appearance.
If disabled, internal bridges may look better but can
settingItems.label: Thick internal bridges

settingItems.description:
In order to reduce the visibility of the seam in a closed loop extrusion, the loop is interrupted and shortened by a specified amount.
This amount can be specified in millimeters or as a percentage of the current extruder diameter. The default value for th
settingItems.label: Seam gap

settingItems.description: The start position to print each part of outer wall.
settingItems.label: Seam position

settingItems.description: Apply scarf joints only to smooth perimeters where traditional seams do not conceal the seams at sharp corners effectively.
settingItems.label: Conditional scarf joint

settingItems.description: The scarf extends to the entire length of the wall.
settingItems.label: Scarf around entire wall

settingItems.description: Use scarf joint for inner walls as well.
settingItems.label: Scarf joint for inner walls

settingItems.description: Length of the scarf. Setting this parameter to zero effectively disables the scarf.
settingItems.label: Scarf length

settingItems.description: Minimum number of segments of each scarf.
settingItems.label: Scarf steps

settingItems.description: This option causes the inner seams to be shifted backwards based on their depth, forming a zigzag pattern.
settingItems.label: Staggered inner seams

settingItems.description:
Controls the density (spacing) of external bridge lines.
Theoretically, 100% means a solid bridge, but due to the tendency of bridge extrusions to sag, 100% may not be sufficient.

- Higher than 100% density (Recommended Max 125%):
  - Pros: Produces smoot
settingItems.label: External bridge density

settingItems.description:
Enable this option to slow down printing in areas where perimeters may have curled upwards.
For example, additional slowdown will be applied when printing overhangs on sharp corners like the front of the Benchy hull, reducing curling which compounds over m
settingItems.label: Slow down for curled perimeters

settingItems.description: Line pattern of bottom surface infill, not bridge infill.
settingItems.label: Bottom surface pattern

settingItems.description: Angle for sparse infill pattern, which controls the start or main direction of line.
settingItems.label: Sparse infill direction

settingItems.description: Line pattern of internal solid infill. if the detect narrow internal solid infill be enabled, the concentric pattern will be used for the small area.
settingItems.label: Internal solid infill pattern

settingItems.description: Angle for solid infill pattern, which controls the start or main direction of line.
settingItems.label: Solid infill direction

settingItems.description: This parameter adds a rotation of solid infill direction to each layer according to the specified template. The template is a comma-separated list of angles in degrees, e.g. '0,90'. The first angle is applied to the first layer, the second angle to the sec
settingItems.label: Solid infill rotation template

settingItems.description: Density of internal sparse infill, 100% turns all sparse infill into solid infill and internal solid infill pattern will be used.
settingItems.label: Sparse infill density

settingItems.description: Line pattern for internal sparse infill.
settingItems.label: Sparse infill pattern

settingItems.description: Rotate the sparse infill direction per layer using a template of angles. Enter comma-separated degrees (e.g., '0,30,60,90'). Angles are applied in order by layer and repeat when the list ends. Advanced syntax is supported: '+5' rotates +5° every layer; '+
settingItems.label: Sparse infill rotation template

settingItems.description: Line pattern of top surface infill.
settingItems.label: Top surface pattern

settingItems.description:
A draft shield is useful to protect an ABS or ASA print from warping and detaching from print bed due to wind draft. It is usually needed only with open frame printers, i.e. without an enclosure.

Enabled = skirt is as tall as the highest printed object. O
settingItems.label: Draft shield

settingItems.description: If enabled, all printing extruders will be primed at the front edge of the print bed at the start of the print.
settingItems.label: Prime all printing extruders

settingItems.description:
Print sequence of the internal (inner) and external (outer) walls.

Use Inner/Outer for best overhangs. This is because the overhanging walls can adhere to a neighbouring perimeter while printing. However, this option results in slightly reduced surface qu
settingItems.label: Walls printing order

settingItems.description: This is the number of solid layers of bottom shell, including the bottom surface layer. When the thickness calculated by this value is thinner than bottom shell thickness, the bottom shell layers will be increased.
settingItems.label: Bottom shell layers

settingItems.description:
Specifies how many consecutive layers share the same ripple phase before the offset is applied.
For example:
- 1 = Layer 1 is printed with the base ripple pattern, then layer 2 is shifted by the configured offset, then layer 3 returns to the base pattern,
settingItems.label: Layers between ripple offset

settingItems.description: Controls how many full cycles of ripples will be added per layer.
settingItems.label: Number of ripples per layer

settingItems.description: Tightens the gyroid wave along the Z (vertical) axis at low infill density to shorten the effective vertical column length and improve Z-axis compression buckling resistance. Filament use is preserved. No effect at ~30% sparse infill density and above. Onl
settingItems.label: Z-buckling bias optimization (experimental)

settingItems.description:
Noise type to use for fuzzy skin generation:
Classic: Classic uniform random noise.
Perlin: Perlin noise, which gives a more consistent texture.
Billow: Similar to perlin noise, but clumpier.
Ridged Multifractal: Ridged noise with sharp, jagged features. C
settingItems.label: Fuzzy skin noise type

settingItems.description: The remaining part of the model contour after removing a certain depth from the surface is called the skeleton. This parameter is used to adjust the density of this section. When two regions have the same sparse infill settings but different skeleton densi
settingItems.label: Skeleton infill density

settingItems.description:
Travel acceleration of first layer.
The percentage value is relative to Travel Acceleration.
settingItems.label: First layer travel

settingItems.description:
Travel jerk of first layer.
The percentage value is relative to Travel Jerk.
settingItems.label: First layer travel

settingItems.description: Using multiple lines for the infill pattern, if supported by infill pattern.
settingItems.label: Fill Multiline

settingItems.description: The portion of the model's outer surface within a certain depth range is called the skin. This parameter is used to adjust the density of this section. When two regions have the same sparse infill settings but different skin densities, this area will not b
settingItems.label: Skin infill density

settingItems.description:
Line width of the Bridge. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.
Recommended to use with a higher Bridge density or Bridge flow ratio.

The maximum value is 100% or the nozzle diameter.
If set to 0, the line width will match the
settingItems.label: Bridge

settingItems.description:
This option can help reduce pillowing on top surfaces in heavily slanted or curved models.
By default, small internal bridges are filtered out and the internal solid infill is printed directly over the sparse infill. This works well in most cases, speeding
settingItems.label: Filter out small internal bridges

settingItems.description: Sparse infill areas smaller than this threshold value are replaced by internal solid infill.
settingItems.label: Minimum sparse infill threshold

settingItems.description: Acceleration of sparse infill. If the value is expressed as a percentage (e.g. 100%), it will be calculated based on the default acceleration.
settingItems.label: Sparse infill

settingItems.description: Density of the first raft or support layer.
settingItems.label: First layer density

settingItems.description: Density of top surface layer. A value of 100% creates a fully solid, smooth top layer. Reducing this value results in a textured top surface, according to the chosen top surface pattern. A value of 0% will result in only the walls on the top layer being cr
settingItems.label: Top surface density

settingItems.description: Adjusts the density of the support structure used to generate the tips of the branches. A higher value results in better overhangs but the supports are harder to remove, thus it is recommended to enable top support interfaces instead of a high branch densi
settingItems.label: Branch Density

settingItems.description: The pattern that will be used when ironing.
settingItems.label: Ironing Pattern

settingItems.description: Cover the top contact layer of the supports with loops. Disabled by default.
settingItems.label: Interface use loop pattern

settingItems.description: Line pattern of support interface. Default pattern for non-soluble support interface is Rectilinear, while default pattern for soluble support interface is Concentric.
settingItems.label: Interface pattern

settingItems.description: The pattern that will be used when ironing.
settingItems.label: Support Ironing Pattern

settingItems.description: The first few layers are printed slower than normal. The speed is gradually increased in a linear fashion over the specified number of layers.
settingItems.label: Number of slow layers

settingItems.description:
Extrude perimeters that have a part over an overhang in the reverse direction on even layers. This alternating pattern can drastically improve steep overhangs.

This setting can also help reduce part warping due to the reduction of stresses in the part wal
settingItems.label: Overhang reversal

settingItems.description:
Apply the reverse perimeters logic only on internal perimeters.

settingItems.label: Reverse only internal perimeters

settingItems.description: Object will be raised by this number of support layers. Use this function to avoid warping when printing ABS.
settingItems.label: Raft layers

settingItems.description: Create additional perimeter paths over steep overhangs and areas where bridges cannot be anchored.
settingItems.label: Extra perimeters on overhangs

settingItems.description: The angle of the infill angled lines. 60° will result in a pure honeycomb.
settingItems.label: Infill overhang angle

settingItems.description: Maximum overhang angle for Lightning infill support propagation.
settingItems.label: Lightning overhang angle

settingItems.description: Modify the geometry to print overhangs without support material.
